question.problem: Which of the following is a representation of the set $S=Z\times {Z}_{0}^{-}$ in the Cartesian plane?
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

$$
A\times B=\{(a,b)\,:\,a\in A,\,b\in B\}
$$

In this case, the set 

$$
S=Z\times {Z}_{0}^{-}
$$

contains every point in ${R}^{2}$ whose $x$-coordinate is an integer number and whose $y$-coordinate is a negative integer or zero..

$$
S=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\in Z,\,y\in {Z}_{0}^{-}\}.
$$

To visualize $S$, consider ${S}_{-1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $-1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is negative integer or zero.

$$
{S}_{-1}=\{(-1,y)\,:\,y\in {Z}_{0}^{-}\}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{-1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14249122/assets/a5d50bdd40efb18b4d29f3e108576e3befcc0d3f3e5b54a0686aeef6e9ffa212.png)

Next, consider ${S}_{1}⊂S$ containing all points whose $x$-coordinate equals $1$ and whose $y$-coordinate is any negative integer or zero.

$$
{S}_{1}=\{(1,y)\,:\,y\in {Z}_{0}^{-}\}.
$$

We can represent ${S}_{1}$ in the plane as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14249122/assets/129cb0ae2a59415a90118030461244ab7f1faa91aba47b5e0e2864323dbfede9.png)

We can create the subsets $…,{S}_{-3},{S}_{-2},{S}_{0},{S}_{2},{S}_{3},…$ similarly. Our Cartesian product $S$ is the *union* of these subsets:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =…\cup {S}_{-3}\cup {S}_{-2}\cup {S}_{-1}\cup {S}_{0}\cup {S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2}\cup {S}_{3}\cup … \\  & ={⋃}_{i\in Z}{S}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can visualize $Z\times {Z}_{0}^{-}$ as the set of points in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14249122/assets/25bd7ebe8087af06fa21e4d5f9878d0e5867630372138bad1af241c1ee270d30.png)
